- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.75) and forecast is below recent low, adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and forecast is above recent high, reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overcorrection.
- If forecast shows sharp spike followed by steep decline, reduce peak value by 5–10% to account for overshoot.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and forecast deviates >3% from 14-day moving average, revert toward mean to avoid mean reversion miss.
- For 30-day horizon, if last 3 forecast values are trending upward but true outcome is flat or declining, reduce final 2–3 values by 2–5% to avoid overextension.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 or 1.00 extremes, apply smoothing filter to avoid overreacting to sentiment noise.
